title: Every new vault type must be added to the SP-BEAM and inherits default bounds, so no rate can be left unbounded by omission
content:
A.3.7.1.3.2 requires that "when new vaults are added to the protocol, they must also be added to the SP-BEAM," and that "unless specified otherwise within the relevant subdocument herein, the SP-BEAM parameters for any newly added Native Vault type shall default to match the parameters defined herein for the ETH-A vault type." A.3.7.1.3.3 states the identical rule for Allocator Vaults, defaulting to ALLOCATOR-SPARK-A.

The pattern is worth naming because it inverts the usual failure mode of parameterized systems. Normally an omission means *absent* configuration — a new vault type simply is not in the module, and either cannot be operated through it or, worse, is operable without bounds. Here an omission means *inherited* configuration, so the safe state is the default state and forgetting to configure a new vault produces conservative behaviour rather than a gap.

The two chosen templates also reveal a deliberate class distinction visible in the parameter tables: Native Vault types default to a `min` of 200 basis points, while Allocator Vaults default to a `min` of 0. Prime Agents borrowing through Allocator Vaults can be charged nothing, whereas end-user Core Vaults always carry a floor rate — consistent with Core Vaults being deprecated and Allocator Vaults being the intended channel for ecosystem liquidity.

The requirement is also a coupling obligation: adding a vault is not complete until its rate is inside the bounded-delegation envelope.
description: New Native Vaults default to the ETH-A parameters and new Allocator Vaults to ALLOCATOR-SPARK-A unless a subdocument says otherwise, making bounded delegation the fallback state.
